data.title: Skip Link
data.tagline: A link that lets keyboard users skip repeated navigation and move to the main content
data.description: A skip link appears when someone starts tabbing through a page and moves focus past repeated header links to the main content. It is not ordinary navigation, and it needs a visible focus state and a working target.

distinctions.label: Anchor navigation
distinctions.explanation: Skip Link is a keyboard shortcut available when entering a page. Anchor is an in-page table of contents that anyone can use.

avoid: Linking to a missing or unclear target
Using it to hide essential navigation

lessonPractice.title: Keyboard users Tab through a long navigation on every page before reaching content. What should be provided?

options.label: Provide a focusable Skip to main content link at page start that targets main
options.feedback: Correct. A skip link lets repeated keyboard users bypass content that is the same on every page.

options.label: Permanently hide main so people do not pass navigation
options.feedback: Hiding main removes the page’s core information for everyone.

options.label: Automatically move everyone to main on page load
options.feedback: Automatic movement interrupts normal navigation; people should choose it when needed.

data.agentPrompt: Add a Skip to main content link first in page order, visible on keyboard focus, targeting the single main region. Ensure the target can receive focus, for example with tabindex="-1" when needed. Press Enter from the link and confirm document.activeElement moves into main; it should not occupy layout during normal pointer browsing.
